subject: FY27 ops & cost scenario planning — kickoff
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: FY27 ops & cost scenario planning — kickoff

Team,

I'm starting the FY27 annual planning work for ops/costs and want to align on a compact scenario process that ties to OKRs. Goals for this thread:

- Agree on 3 scenarios (base, upside, downside) with explicit assumptions for capacity, Dedicated commitments, and GPU cost per token.
- Surface OKR implications (throughput targets, latency SLOs, cost/unit targets).
- Lock a short timeline so org teams can model impacts before the QBR.

Attached is a first-pass template (FY27_scenarios_template_v0.1.xlsx). Please do the following by EOD Mon (Nov 22):

1) Fill the "assumptions" tab with your org's primary drivers (capacity, committed nodes, expected growth).
2) Add topline ARR / renewal risk notes (Marissa) and major deal timings that could change capacity needs.
3) Provide a short note on any technical constraints (Ben).

I propose a 60-min sync on Tue Nov 23 at 10am PT to review consolidated scenarios and confirm owners. If that doesn't work, suggest alternatives.

Thanks — clear owners and short iterations here will make the QBR work a lot easier.

- Grace
Grace O'Connor
VP, Operations & Planning
Redwood Inference

Attachments: FY27_scenarios_template_v0.1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FY27 ops & cost scenario planning — kickoff

Grace — thanks for kicking this off. Couple of clarifying Qs before I populate the template:

- Should finance include reserved capacity discounts and committed Dedicated contracts as part of the base case, or treat those as an adjustment line? My preference is to show committed spend in the base case and model optional bursts under upside.
- Do you want us to include customer-cost passthroughs (marketplace fees/3rd-party infra) or keep this strictly Redwood-ops?

I'll fill in the topline cost assumptions (GPU $/hr equivalency and APAC/region deltas) once that's clarified.

Aditya
Chief Financial Officer
Redwood Inference

Adding a sales lens:

- We'll model ARR scenarios tied to three pipeline outcomes: conservative (no large renewals), expected (90% renewal with two expansion deals), and aggressive (three expansions + enterprise deals). I'll drop a pipeline_snapshot_nov19.csv into the Drive link.
- Important to separate renewal risk by account tier — small renewals shouldn't drive Dedicated capacity, but two enterprise renewals in H1 would.

Timing: two things — if we want useful input for QBR decks, please let us finalize assumptions by Nov 24 so GTM can model revenue impact and recommended pricing levers.

Marissa

Quick infra notes to include in assumptions:

- GPU pricing: spot vs committed pricing trends look favorable for H1 27 but expect supply volatility that could hit spot rates by ~15-20% in a downside scenario. Suggest modeling a +20% cost shock in downside.
- KV / cache savings: assume a 10% effective token reduction for customers with prefix caching enabled; that should be modeled as a levers row.
- Dedicated capacity: plan one "buffer" cluster for enterprise bursts in upside — cost can be amortized across renewals, but include a 3-month lead time for provisioning in timelines.

I'll add a short assumptions tab in the template with these numbers. If helpful, I can estimate per-token delta under the three scenarios by Friday.

— Ben
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — great, actionable feedback. Short summary and next steps: 

Decisions / Assumptions agreed (for now):
- Base case: include committed Dedicated contracts and recurring committed spend; model optional bursts as an upside line.
- Cost shock: downside +20% GPU price sensitivity to capture supply volatility (Ben to provide per-token delta by Fri Nov 26).
- Savings: assume 10% token reduction from caching for eligible customers.

Action items:
- Aditya: populate finance assumptions (reserved discounts, passthroughs) in the template — due Nov 24.
- Marissa: upload pipeline_snapshot_nov19.csv and tag accounts with renewal risk tiers — due Nov 24.
- Ben: provide per-token delta and provisioning lead-time confirmation (due Nov 26).
- Grace (me): consolidate and share the combined scenario deck and short one-pager for the QBR by Nov 29.

I've updated the Drive file (link above) and scheduled the review sync for Tue Nov 23, 10am PT; calendar invite is live. If any of the owners need to shift dates, flag now.

Thanks — let's keep the inputs tight and focused.

- Grace
VP, Operations & Planning
Redwood Inference
